<text>
Summary of proposals and positions (ideology removed)

- European Union and currency
  - Withdraw from the EU; repeal the European Communities Act 1972.
  - Negotiate trade agreements with European states and others; keep the pound permanently.
  - Maintain Bank of England interest-rate independence.

- Economy, trade, and regulation
  - Pursue global free trade, deepen ties with Commonwealth and North America.
  - Large-scale deregulation, prioritising small and medium-sized enterprises; review metrication and abattoir rules.
  - Simplify and reduce taxes: raise the income tax threshold to remove ~1 million low earners from tax, reform inheritance and capital gains taxes, consider replacing VAT with a retail sales tax after EU exit.
  - Oppose tax harmonisation.

- Independence Dividend (estimated ~£20bn annually)
  - Savings from ending EU budget contributions and gains from deregulation and growth.
  - Planned allocations include: agriculture (£2bn), regional support (£1bn), state pension uplift (£2.8bn), elderly care (£0.5bn), restoring frozen expat pensions (£0.3bn), tax changes (£2.7bn total), NHS (£2bn) plus nursing pay (£0.5bn), 30,000 more teachers (£1.2bn), 25,000 more police (£0.8bn), fuel duty cut (9p/litre; ~£3.7bn), defence (£2.5bn).

- Health and social care
  - Increase NHS funding; restore clearer hospital management roles (e.g., matron-style leadership), reduce bureaucracy, focus on infection control and patient care.
  - Improve nurse pay and retention; rebalance training toward practical competence; recruit internationally where needed.
  - Review and simplify social services; reduce bureaucracy and focus on practical outcomes.

- Welfare and pensions
  - Simplify benefits to reduce fraud and administration; ensure work always pays.
  - Consider basic income-style support for specific groups to aid re-entry to work.
  - Raise state pension by £5/week; increase elderly care funding; restore full pensions to affected expatriates.
  - Explore partial diversion of National Insurance into personal pension funds (grandfathering existing pensioners).

- Education
  - Allow selection/streaming; target class sizes under 25; hire more teachers; elevate technical/vocational routes; consider vouchers; encourage specialist and single-sex or faith options where desired.
  - Reform teacher training toward proven methods; address discipline and attainment gaps.
  - Protect school sports and halt sale of playing fields.
  - Support independent funding models for higher education; encourage private universities with scholarships; treat overseas students equally by origin.

- Transport and environment
  - Integrated transport; case-by-case approach to ownership/privatisation; oppose part-sale of London Underground.
  - Reduce fuel duty; fund bypasses, route upgrades, maintenance, cycle lanes; adjust vehicle tax by emissions.
  - Decentralise environmental enforcement to local authorities; strengthen monitoring of pollution-related health impacts.
  - Strong GMO labelling and protections; encourage renewables (biofuels, wave, wind, solar, hydrogen).

- Home affairs, justice, and rights
  - Protect jury trial and common-law safeguards; oppose EU-wide legal and policing integration.
  - Repeal and reenact the Human Rights Act to align with domestic legal tradition.
  - Increase police numbers; prioritise visible, community-linked policing; use rehabilitation and non-custodial sentences for non-violent offences; “life means life” for the most serious crimes.

- Immigration and asylum
  - Skills-based immigration model; equalise treatment for family reunification compared with non-EU countries.
  - Speed up asylum processing with reception centres; tighten monitoring; prioritise first safe country principles; seek reform of the 1951 Refugee Convention.

- Agriculture and fisheries
  - Replace CAP with national policy; introduce voluntary Land Management Contracts paying for agreed environmental and land-use outcomes; support organics and higher welfare; assist young farmers; enable diversification and farmers’ markets.
  - Amend right-to-roam to reflect local conditions.
  - Exit the Common Fisheries Policy; exclusive national control up to 200 miles under international law; create recovery zones and ban damaging methods; allow access via bilateral agreements.

- Defence and foreign affairs
  - Increase defence spending on personnel and equipment; prioritise NATO; leave EU defence structures.
  - Pursue cost-effective procurement, including from the US.
  - Refocus aid toward communities, with governance and freedom conditions.

- Constitution and governance
  - Enact a UK Bill of Rights preventing transfer of sovereignty without consent.
  - Strengthen Parliament over the executive; empower select committees; review quangos.
  - Oppose regionalisation; consider a further Welsh referendum; address West Lothian question; restore county-based local government; enable citizen-initiated local referenda with an impartial referendum commission.
</text>
